requirements: three true round-arched timber apparatus openings with deep masonry returns
steep slate mansard with bounded dormers and a closed hipped crown
corner bell cupola with open arcade, copper dome and weathervane
Treat the approved orthographic crest's warm aged limestone as the building-level exterior masonry authority.

Use that one limestone family for wall cores and returns, coursed ashlar, quoins, arches, strings, cornices, dormer masonry, cupola columns, and the crest carrier; vary dressing and relief only by physical role.
Preserve the source-specific slate, oak, copper, iron, glass, geometry, openings, and registered crest without alteration.
Dressed limestone and exposed wall returns must share the crest-authorized warm hue; no pale-grey or white secondary stone family may remain.

Use the crest-derived shadow-neutral dressed-limestone specimen for every exposed core, return, quoin, arch, string, cornice, dormer surround, masonry roof attachment, cupola column, crest carrier, and support.
Frame left, right, rear, and rear-side evidence from grade to finial with the complete footprint and neutral margin.
Embed every side dormer body through the mansard roof plane so its lower cheeks are physically captured by the roof rather than floating outside it.
Give every side dormer a closed limestone gable field, seated slate gable roof, and bounded flashing/apron at the roof intersection.
Prove the dormer-to-mansard contact in both whole-side views, aerial, and a dedicated oblique dormer-contact close-up.
Cut every side-dormer opening completely through the integrated dormer body; no residual exterior masonry skin may cover the sash or pane.
Seat the limestone reveal, oak sash, glass, and occupied-depth layer inside the outward dormer face while preserving the roof-plane penetration, closed gable, and flashing contact.
